system_prompt: You design levels for a small tower-defense game (Cannons) and test your own design hypotheses by simulation before trusting them. Be specific and falsifiable: state a hypothesis, then build ONE level designed to be a sharp test of it (not a generic level).
user_prompt:
Level JSON schema (must match exactly):
{
  "levelNumber": <int>,
  "password": "<1 uppercase letter + 4 digits, e.g. Q1234>",
  "isHard": <bool>,
  "filas": [
    {"cuadros": [{"index": <0-4>, "tipo": <1-4>, "hp": <1-10>}, ...]},
    ...
  ]
}
Each "fila" is one wave/round. "cuadros" may be an empty list (a breathing-room
round with no pirates). "index" is the column (0=right .. 4=left). "tipo" 1-3
are visually-different normal pirates (same difficulty), 4 marks the last
pirate of the level (use it exactly once, on the final fila that has any
pirates). Max 5 cuadros per fila (one per column, no two pirates share a
column+round).


Confirmed rules so far from previous cycles:
- **Hypothesis:**  
A final pirate (tipo 4) with HP = 2 can be cleared without any merges if the pirate directly in front of it (same column, immediately preceding fila) has HP = 1 **and** there is at least one empty fila separating them, allowing the final pirate to receive two separate base‑damage hits (one in the empty fila’s wave and one in its own wave). => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-23)
- **Hypothesis:**  
If the pirates in a single column have strictly decreasing HP values from the topmost pirate to the bottommost pirate, the level is always winnable without performing any merges, even when the total HP in that column exceeds the total number of filas in the level. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-23)
- A final pirate (tipo 4) with HP = 2 can be cleared without any merges even when the pirate directly in front of it in the same column also has HP = 2, as long as there is at least one empty fila separating them (allowing the final pirate to receive two separate base‑damage hits after the blocker is killed). => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-23)
- **Hypothesis:**  
The cannon’s base damage of 1 is applied on every wave, even in waves that contain no pirates; therefore empty filas before a pirate appears still contribute damage toward reducing that pirate’s HP. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
A final pirate (tipo 4) with HP = k can be eliminated without any merges if there are at least k consecutive empty filas directly above it in the same column, because the cannon’s base damage = 1 is applied on every wave, including empty ones. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
The cannon can fire at only one column per wave (i.e., each wave delivers a single point of damage to a single chosen column). Consequently, a level that places two or more pirates with total HP > (number of filas) in different columns becomes unwinnable without merges, even though each column individually would receive enough damage if the cannon could hit all columns simultaneously. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
A final pirate (tipo 4) does **not** receive the cannon’s base damage = 1 during empty filas that occur before its own fila; it can only be damaged starting from its own wave. Consequently, a level that places a final pirate with HP > 1 after only empty filas should be unwinnable without performing a merge. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
If, in any single column, the sum of the HP of all pirates from the first (topmost) pirate in that column down to the final fila exceeds the number of filas spanned by that segment (i.e., the count of rows from that first pirate to the last fila inclusive), then the level cannot be cleared without performing at least one merge, even when each individual pirate’s HP is low enough to be killable on its own. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
If a column contains pirates whose HP values are not non‑increasing (i.e., a lower pirate has higher HP than a pirate above it), the level can be unwinnable without any merges even when each pirate’s HP does not exceed the number of filas remaining from its own fila to the final fila. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
Pirates of tipo 3 are immune to the cannon’s base damage = 1; they can be eliminated only by merging with another pirate (i.e., a level that contains a solo tipo 3 pirate must require a merge to be winnable). => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis**  
When a pirate that blocks the line of fire is killed in a wave, the cannon’s damage continues in that same wave to affect the next pirate in the same column (i.e., damage can pass through a killed blocker within the same wave). => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis**  
A pirate of tipo 2 cannot be eliminated using only the cannon’s base damage = 1, even when there are enough waves (filas) to deal its total HP; it requires at least one merge unless its HP ≤ 2. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
A final pirate (tipo 4) with HP = 1 cannot be eliminated without performing a merge if the pirate directly in front of it (same column, immediately preceding fila) is of tipo 3, because tipo 3 pirates are immune to the cannon’s base damage and therefore block the line of fire permanently. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis**  
A pirate (of tipo 1, 2, or 4) with HP = k cannot be eliminated without performing a merge if the number of remaining filas from the wave in which it first appears (including that wave) is fewer than k, since the cannon can inflict at most one point of damage to its column per wave. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
A pirate of type 1, 2, or 4 does **not** receive any cannon damage during empty filas that occur before the wave in which it first appears; its HP can only be reduced starting from its own fila onward. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)

Seed hypotheses worth stress-testing (human-authored guesses, not verified by
your own play — confirm, refine, or overturn them):
- With cannon base damage 1, a lone pirate needs HP <= 3 to be beatable without
  any merge.
- Two pirates in the same column on consecutive rows block each other's shots.
- Merge budget roughly scales with number of rows minus ~5.

Propose ONE hypothesis (1-2 sentences) about what makes a level winnable or fun
that isn't already confirmed above, then ONE level (JSON) built specifically to
test it sharply. Respond with the hypothesis as plain text, then the JSON in a
single ```json code block.

**Hypothesis:**  
If, in a single column, the sum of the HP of all pirates from the first pirate in that column down to the final fila equals the number of filas spanned by that segment, the level can be cleared without performing any merges.
